lessons.unit: Unit 1: Refining our recitation
lessons.title: Minor mistakes: polishing our recitation
objectives: Distinguish major mistakes from minor mistakes
Name common minor mistakes
Use a checklist to improve a recitation

keywords.def: an error against a rule of tajweed that does not change a letter
an error that changes a letter or a vowel

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and basmalah.
Give an example of a major mistake from Year 3 (qul / kul).
How many counts for natural madd? For muttasil?

teach.heading: Two levels of mistakes
bullets: Major: a letter or vowel is changed
Minor: a rule is missed or weak
teach.note: Recap Year 3. Explain that major mistakes are corrected first, then minor ones. Make clear that every learner makes minor mistakes and that tajweed is a lifelong journey. Mention the hadith narrated by Aisha (RA) in Bukhari and Muslim about the reward of the one who recites with difficulty.

teach.heading: Common minor mistakes
bullets: Missing ghunnah or cutting it short
Stretching madd too little or too much
teach.note: Demonstrate each mistake on a word and ask the pupils to identify it. Use words from known surahs: النَّاسِ (ghunnah), الْعَالَمِينَ (madd), أَحَدٌ (qalqalah), الصَّمَدُ (heavy letter).

teach.heading: The checklist
teach.note: Pupils copy this four-point checklist. Explain they will use it for peer feedback this term. Emphasise adab: gentle, private, encouraging corrections.

teach.heading: Peer feedback with adab
bullets: End with a dua for each other
teach.note: Model a feedback conversation. Pair up and practise on Al-Fatihah. Model kind language: 'Your madd was lovely, can you add ghunnah on إِنَّ?'

practice: Give one example of a major mistake.
Which minor mistake is easy to miss in النَّاسِ?
independent: Listen to a recording with errors and tick the checklist
Peer feedback on Al-Fatihah using the checklist
Record yourself and list one strength and one target
exit: What is the difference between a major and a minor mistake?
Name two items on the checklist.
lessons.homework: Recite Surat An-Nas to a family member and ask them to give you one thing to improve.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: checklist with icons and sentence stems for feedback. Stretch: write a personal target for the term.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Refining our recitation
lessons.title: Noon sakinah and tanween: complete review
objectives: Recall all four rules and their letters
Apply the rules to phrases quickly
Recite with the correct ghunnah length

keywords.def: clear, before the six throat letters

starter: What is iqlab? Which letter causes it?
Name the idgham letters (yanmu) and explain.

teach.heading: Four rules, 28 letters
bullets: Izhar: ء ه ع ح غ خ (6)
Idgham: ي ر م ل و ن (6)
teach.note: Pupils fill in the table from memory. Check the total: 6 + 6 + 1 + 15 = 28. Remind pupils that idgham needs two words. Ask: which rule is the biggest group?

teach.heading: Read and decide
teach.note: Call out each phrase and pupils say the rule. Move on to another short list. Ask for reasons: what is the next letter?

teach.heading: Ghunnah length
bullets: Same in idgham, iqlab and ikhfa
teach.note: Tap two counts. Common minor mistake: cutting ghunnah. Model both too short and correct. Pupils copy.

teach.heading: Ikhfa: heavy or light
bullets: Ikhfa before heavy letters is fuller
ص ض ط ظ ق - fuller
teach.note: Contrast مِن قَبْلِكَ (full) with مِن شَرِّ (light). Pupils feel the back of the tongue stay raised before ق. Keep the length at two counts in both.

practice: Name the rule in مِن بَعْدِ.
Which rule applies in مِن شَرِّ?
independent: Sort 15 phrases into the four rules
Fill in the rules table from memory
Read Al-Falaq and Al-Asr and label every noon sakinah and tanween
exit: How many letters does ikhfa have?
Why does idgham need two words?
lessons.homework: Make a rules poster for noon sakinah and tanween and teach it to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: colour-coded table with example phrases. Stretch: find all four rules in one short surah.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Refining our recitation
lessons.title: Qalqalah: three levels of echo
objectives: Name the qalqalah letters
Hear the weak, strong and strongest echo
Apply qalqalah in words

keywords.def: an echo on ق ط ب ج د when they are quiet
the stronger echo when stopping on the letter

teach.heading: Remember the letters
teach.note: Revise the five letters and the idea of the bounce. Ask: why must the letter be quiet? The echo is a result of the sukoon.

teach.heading: Level 1: in the middle
bullets: The letter has a sukoon inside a word or ayah
teach.note: Examples: يَجْعَلْ (Al-Fil 105:2) and الْأَبْتَرُ (Al-Kawthar 108:3, qalqalah on the baa). Model a short, light bounce. Pupils echo.

teach.heading: Level 2: when stopping
bullets: Stopping on the letter makes the echo stronger
teach.note: Examples: أَحَدٌ (Al-Ikhlas) and الْفَلَقِ (Al-Falaq 113:1) when stopping. Model a clear, stronger bounce.

teach.heading: Level 3: strongest
bullets: Stopping on a letter with shaddah
teach.note: Say وَتَبَّ with a very clear bounce, still short. Common mistake: adding a vowel (e.g. 'tabba-a'). Pupils practise hand gestures: low, medium, high bounce.

practice: Which level of echo is on وَتَبَّ?
independent: Find qalqalah in Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and Al-Fil and label each level
Practise the three levels with hand gestures
Recite Al-Ikhlas stopping at each ayah
exit: What is the strongest level of qalqalah?
Why must the echo not be a vowel?
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Ikhlas and Al-Falaq every day, checking that each echo is the right strength.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: three-level echo diagram and audio. Stretch: find a qalqalah letter in your current memorisation.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Refining our recitation
lessons.title: Madd review: counts and signs
objectives: Name the main types of madd
Give the count for each type
Read examples at the right length

keywords.def: hamza in the same word: 4-5 counts

starter: How many counts is natural madd?
Which madd comes before a hamza in a different word?

teach.heading: The ladder
teach.note: Draw the ladder on the board. Pupils tap each length. Ask which are the shortest and which are the longest.

teach.heading: Examples from the Qur'an
teach.note: Use known examples. Pupils say the type and count. Include one natural madd to compare.

teach.heading: When we stop
bullets: Leen: soft waaw or yaa after fathah: خَوْفٍ
teach.note: Practise stopping at the end of each ayah in Quraysh. Model the three lengths and pick one for the class. Explain that consistent length is more important than which one you pick.

teach.heading: Use the signs
bullets: The sign ~ marks a longer madd
teach.note: Pupils mark madd on a printed page with the type and count above each. Check: where are the longest madds?

practice: Give the count for madd lazim.
What is the difference between muttasil and munfasil?
independent: Mark every madd on Quraysh with type and count
Race: sort 12 words into the right madd
Recite Al-Fatihah with accurate madd lengths
exit: Which madd happens only when stopping?
lessons.homework: Mark all madd in Al-Fatihah on a printed copy and recite with the correct lengths.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: ladder diagram with colours. Stretch: explain why 'arid is called temporary.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Surat Al-Masad
lessons.title: Surat Al-Masad
objectives: Recite Al-Masad accurately
Apply qalqalah and other rules
Understand the surah's message
starter: Name the three levels of qalqalah.

teach.heading: The surah
bullets: مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ
teach.note: This surah is about Abu Lahab, an uncle of the Prophet ﷺ who opposed him. It is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari that it was revealed after Abu Lahab spoke against the Prophet ﷺ when he called the people to Islam on Mount Safa. Chunk and echo.

teach.heading: Ayat 3-5
teach.note: Meaning: he will enter a blazing fire, and his wife who carried firewood, with a rope of palm fibre around her neck. Keep the description measured for pupils. Chunk and echo.

teach.heading: Tajweed to find
teach.note: Pupils label the rules. In ayah 5 the noon of مِن meets meem: idgham with ghunnah. Also حَمَّالَةَ has meem with shaddah: ghunnah. Practise the strongest echo on وَتَبَّ.

teach.heading: Lesson from the surah
bullets: Wealth and status cannot save us
teach.note: Link to مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ: money did not help him. Ask: what does help us on the Day of Judgement? Faith, good deeds, and Allah's mercy.

independent: Read Al-Masad in pairs, labelling qalqalah and ghunnah
Memorise ayat 1-2 with listen/read/cover
Recite individually to teacher
exit: Name one qalqalah letter in the surah.
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Masad daily and learn ayat 1-3 by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and a rule highlighter sheet. Stretch: learn all five ayat.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Surat Ad-Duha
lessons.title: Surat Ad-Duha: ayat 1-5
objectives: Recite Ad-Duha ayat 1-5 accurately
Understand the comfort in the surah
Find tajweed rules in the ayat

teach.heading: The surah
teach.note: Explain that this surah comforted the Prophet ﷺ after a pause in the revelation, as reported in the hadith collections. Chunk and echo ayat 1-2. Heavy Daad in وَالضُّحَىٰ.

teach.heading: Ayat 3-5
teach.note: Meaning: your Lord has not abandoned you nor hated you; the next life is better for you than this one; and your Lord will give you until you are pleased. Chunk and echo. Ask: what comfort does Allah give?

teach.heading: Rules to find
teach.note: Pupils find the tanween before laam. No ghunnah when the next letter is laam or raa. Check the heavy letter ض and the full-mouth sound.

teach.heading: Memorise it
teach.note: Revise the three-step routine. Memorise ayat 1-3 today; 4-5 next lesson. Pair test: tick the checklist from lesson 1.

practice: Which letter is heavy in وَالضُّحَىٰ?
independent: Read ayat 1-5 in pairs using the checklist
Memorise ayat 1-3, then 4-5
Individual recitation
exit: What does ayah 3 tell us about Allah?
Name the idgham rule in ayah 4.
lessons.homework: Recite Ad-Duha ayat 1-5 daily and learn them by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and translation cards. Stretch: explain ayah 5 in your own words.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Surat Ad-Duha
lessons.title: Surat Ad-Duha: ayat 6-11 and recital
objectives: Recite Ad-Duha ayat 6-11 accurately
Understand the commands of kindness
Recite the whole surah with correct rules

teach.heading: Ayat 6-8
teach.note: Meaning: Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter? And find you lost and guide you? And find you in need and make you rich? Chunk and echo. Rules: qalqalah in يَجِدْكَ; madd badal in فَآوَىٰ.

teach.heading: Ayat 9-11
teach.note: Meaning: do not oppress the orphan, do not scold the one who asks, and speak of your Lord's blessing. Madd muttasil in السَّائِلَ. Ask: how should we treat people in need?

teach.heading: Tajweed check
teach.note: Pupils find and label. Revise that ayat end with madd (alif maqsura): stop and stretch two counts when reciting. Practise stopping at each ayah.

teach.heading: Putting it into action
bullets: Be gentle with people who ask
teach.note: Discuss practical ways: giving sadaqah, speaking kindly, thanking Allah. Pupils choose one action for the week.

independent: Read ayat 6-11 and label the tajweed rules
Memorise ayat 6-8, then 9-11
Recite the whole surah to a partner
exit: What does Allah tell us to do for the orphan?
Name one tajweed rule in ayat 9-11.
lessons.homework: Recite the whole of Ad-Duha daily and do one act of kindness from the surah.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: translation cards and chunked audio. Stretch: write a short reflection on the three blessings in ayat 6-8.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Surat Ad-Duha
lessons.title: Ad-Duha: reflecting and reciting with understanding
objectives: Explain what tadabbur means
Ask simple questions of an ayah
Recite Ad-Duha confidently with correct tajweed

keywords.def: thinking deeply about the meaning of the Qur'an

starter: Recite Ad-Duha from memory with a partner.
Name two tajweed rules from the surah.

teach.heading: What is tadabbur?
bullets: Tadabbur means thinking about the Qur'an
teach.note: Read the ayah meaning: Do they not reflect on the Qur'an? Explain that reciting well and thinking about meaning go together. Ask: what do we do when we understand something? We act on it.

teach.heading: Four questions
bullets: How did the Prophet ﷺ feel?
What can I thank Allah for?
teach.note: Model each question on ayah 3: Allah has not left you. Ask: how might the Prophet ﷺ feel after hearing this? Then connect to pupils' own worries.

teach.heading: Ad-Duha and hope
bullets: Allah did not abandon His Messenger
He gave shelter, guidance and provision
He tells us to be kind in return
teach.note: Pupils link ayat 6-8 to the commands in ayat 9-11. Show the pattern: Allah gave, so we give. Ask: what is the link between thanks and kindness?

teach.heading: Recital
bullets: Stop at the end of each ayah
teach.note: Pupils recite in turn or in breakout pairs. Listen for one strength and one target. Close with a short dua for steadfastness with the Qur'an.

independent: Write one answer to each of the four questions for ayah 5
Recite Ad-Duha to a partner and give feedback with the checklist
Individual recitation to the teacher
exit: What does ayah 3 tell the Prophet ﷺ?
Name one thing Ad-Duha asks us to do.
lessons.homework: Recite Ad-Duha daily and write two sentences about how it makes you feel and what you will do.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: question stems and picture prompts. Stretch: compare Ad-Duha with Ash-Sharh (94) in a short paragraph.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Ghashiyah, the makharij and the rules of laam
lessons.title: Surat Al-Ghashiyah 88:1-5: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: The surah opens with a question: 'Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming?' Why might Allah begin with a question?
objectives: To memorise Al-Ghashiyah 88:1-5 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 88:1-5 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 88:1-5 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 88:1-5 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: thinking about the Day of Judgement and preparing for it with good deeds

keywords.def: the Overwhelming: a name of the Day of Judgement

hook.text: The surah opens with a question: 'Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming?' Why might Allah begin with a question?
hook.a: A question makes us stop and listen. Al-Ghashiyah is a name for the Day of Judgement, which will overwhelm everyone.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming (event)?' (Al-Ghashiyah 88:1). The surah describes two groups on the Day of Judgement and asks us to look at Allah's signs (88:17 to 20).

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Ghashiyah 88:1-5
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 88:1-5 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ٱلْغَٰشِيَةِ (١) وُجُوهٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَٰشِعَةٌ (٢) عَامِلَةٌۭ نَّاصِبَةٌۭ (٣) تَصْلَىٰ نَارًا حَامِيَةًۭ (٤) تُسْقَىٰ مِنْ عَيْنٍ ءَانِيَةٍۢ (٥)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: This is a translation of the meaning, not the Qur'an itself
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming [event]?
[Some] faces, that Day, will be humbled,
They will [enter to] burn in an intensely hot Fire.
They will be given drink from a boiling spring.

teach.heading: Tajweed spotlight in today's ayat
teach.note: Point to each word in the mushaf. Pupils say the rule before you do.

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Full mouth; the laam of al- is clear

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 88:1-5 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Teacher recites one ayah (talaqqi)
Pupils listen, mics muted, eyes on the words
Mics on in turn: three pupils repeat in register order
Teacher corrects one point for each
Whole class repeats softly, then moves to the next ayah

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: Al-Ghashiyah (the Overwhelming) is a name for ...
check.why: The surah describes the faces on that Day (88:2 to 16): it is the Day of Judgement.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-Ghashiyah 88:1-5 together, ayah by ayah.
practice.a: The class recites 88:1-5 together without the mushaf.
practice.model: I do: chunk 88:1-5. Ayah 1: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 2 the same way. Then link: recite 1 and 2 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

practice.a: izhar

independent.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 88:1-5 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: On the pupil PDF, write the meaning of 88:2 in your own words.
independent.a: On that Day some faces will be humbled (lowered in fear).

independent.q: Find two izhar examples in 88:1 to 5 and name the throat letters.
independent.a: نَارًا حَامِيَةًۭ (ح), مِنْ عَيْنٍ (ع), عَيْنٍ ءَانِيَةٍۢ (ء).

exit.q: Al-Ghashiyah 88:2: «وُجُوهٌۭ ...» Which word comes next?
exit.a: يَوْمَئِذٍ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: The surah opens with a question: 'Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming?' Why might Allah begin with a question?
exit.a: A question makes us stop and listen. Al-Ghashiyah is a name for the Day of Judgement, which will overwhelm everyone.

lessons.homework: Recite Al-Ghashiyah 88:1-5 to a parent three times a day and revise Surahs 114 to 89 on the rota (today's group); tick the portal revision log each day.
lessons.send: SEND: shorter chunks (one ayah), the pupil PDF with each word spaced, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: link to the next ayat and explain one rule to the class.

lessons.title: Makharij: the empty space and the throat
lessons.bigQuestion: Put your hand on your throat and say 'aa', then ''a' (ع). Which one do you feel? Where does each sound start?
objectives: To understand where the madd letters and the six throat letters are made
successCriteria: All: say which letters come from the jawf (empty space)
Most: place the six throat letters in the deepest, middle and nearest parts
Some: explain why mixing ع and ء changes a word
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: how sound is made by vibration (Year 4 sound)
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: gratitude for the tongue, lips and voice Allah gave us (90:8 to 9)

keywords.def: the exit point where a letter's sound is made (plural makharij, مخارج)
the empty space of the mouth and throat

hook.text: Put your hand on your throat and say 'aa', then ''a' (ع). Which one do you feel? Where does each sound start?
hook.a: 'Aa' flows from the empty space of the mouth and throat (jawf); ع is pressed in the middle of the throat.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Did We not make for him two eyes, and a tongue and two lips?' (Al-Balad 90:8 to 9). Our mouth and throat are gifts we use to recite His words.

starter.q: Recite Al-Ghashiyah 88:2 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: Five areas where letters are made
teach.note: Bismillah. Makharij (مخارج) are the exit points of the letters. Today: the empty space and the throat.

teach.heading: The jawf: madd letters
teach.note: The madd letters have no fixed point; the sound ends when the breath ends. They are stretched two counts.

teach.heading: The throat: three parts
teach.note: Say each pair slowly; pupils feel the throat with a hand.

teach.heading: Common mistake
teach.note: In English we often drop ع and ح. Model the difference with عَيْن and أَيْن.

misconception.wrong: عَيْنٍ said like 'ayn' with a hamza
misconception.right: Press the middle of the throat for ع: 'ayn

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: Where is ع (ayn) made?
check.why: ع and ح are from the middle of the throat. The lips make ب م و ف; the tongue tip makes letters like ت د.

practice.q: Say عَيْنٍ ءَانِيَةٍۢ (88:5) and name where each first letter comes from.
practice.a: ع: middle of the throat; ء: deepest part of the throat.
practice.model: I do: عَ: I press the middle of my throat. ءَا: the deepest part, then the alif flows from the jawf. 'ayn-in aaniyah.

practice.q: Which letters come from the deepest part?
practice.a: ء ه

independent.q: Makharij map (pupil PDF): label the throat diagram with ء ه ع ح غ خ. Today's rota group recites 88:1 to 5 to the teacher in turn.
independent.a: Deepest ء ه; middle ع ح; nearest the mouth غ خ.
independent.model: The teacher labels the first: ء at the deepest part, near the chest.

independent.q: Extend: write one word from 88:1 to 5 for each throat part.
independent.a: ء or ه: هَلْ (88:1); ع or ح: عَامِلَةٌ (88:3); غ or خ: ٱلْغَٰشِيَةِ (88:1).

independent.q: Stretch: why are the throat letters the izhar letters?
independent.a: They are far from where the noon is made (the tongue tip), so the noon stays clear.

exit.q: Madd letters come from ...
exit.a: the jawf (empty space)

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Put your hand on your throat and say 'aa', then ''a' (ع). Which one do you feel? Where does each sound start?
exit.a: 'Aa' flows from the empty space of the mouth and throat (jawf); ع is pressed in the middle of the throat.

lessons.homework: Say ء ه ع ح غ خ to a parent with a hand on your throat; recite 88:1 to 5; tick the revision log.
lessons.send: SEND: rule card with letters in colour, the pupil PDF with examples spaced out, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: find and explain an example in a surah not on the slides.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Ghashiyah 88:6-11: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: Imagine a garden where you never hear a single bad word. What would that feel like?
objectives: To memorise Al-Ghashiyah 88:6-11 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 88:6-11 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 88:6-11 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 88:6-11 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Moral: good speech; Paradise has no bad words, so we practise that now

hook.text: Imagine a garden where you never hear a single bad word. What would that feel like?
hook.a: Peaceful and happy: Allah describes Paradise as a high garden where no idle or bad speech is heard (88:10 to 11).

islamicLink.text: Allah describes the people of Paradise: 'Faces, that Day, will show pleasure, with their effort satisfied, in an elevated garden, wherein they will hear no unsuitable speech' (Al-Ghashiyah 88:8 to 11).

lessons.title: The laam of al-: sun letters and moon letters
lessons.bigQuestion: We say 'ash-shams' (the sun) but 'al-qamar' (the moon). Why does the 'l' sometimes disappear?
objectives: To understand when the laam of al- (ال) is said clearly and when it merges into the next letter
successCriteria: All: sort words into sun and moon letters

lessons.crossCurricular: English: the definite article 'the' and Arabic al-

keywords.def: sun letters: the laam of al- is not said, the next letter doubles
moon letters: the laam of al- is said clearly
the sign that doubles a letter

hook.text: We say 'ash-shams' (the sun) but 'al-qamar' (the moon). Why does the 'l' sometimes disappear?
hook.a: Before sun letters the laam merges into the next letter (which gets a shaddah); before moon letters it is said clearly.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And the sun runs to its resting place' and 'the moon, We have determined for it phases' (Ya-Sin 36:38 to 39). The Arabic names for the sun and moon give the two rules their names.

teach.heading: Two kinds of al-
teach.note: Bismillah. 'The sun' (ٱلشَّمْسُ) and 'the moon' (ٱلْقَمَرُ) give the rules their names. Fourteen letters each.

hook.text: The same letter laam can be silent, clear, heavy or light. How can one letter have four ways to be said?

exit.a: قُرْءَانٌۭ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: How can we be sure the Qur'an we read today has not been changed?
exit.a: Allah says it is 'an honoured Qur'an in a Preserved Slate' (85:21 to 22): He protects it.
